current_policy.name: destination_wins_array
behavior: preserve destination array as a whole when template and destination both define an array
do not interleave template and destination elements
do not element-match template and destination arrays

old_array_element_claims.old_claim: array elements with matching IDs or similar structure are paired
object array elements can be matched by structural key overlap
array values can be scored by length ratio for fuzzy matching

example.concern: comments attached to matched, inserted, removed, or retained array elements

old_array_element_claims.old_claim: JSONC array merge should preserve comments around array elements

decision.reason: The active JSON conformance contract explicitly preserves destination arrays whole and forbids element matching. Old element matching can only return as a separately named policy with fixtures and diagnostics.

future_fixture_requirements.required_contract: objects in arrays can match by configured identity key when the element policy is enabled
template-only elements are inserted, skipped, or reported according to explicit policy
destination-only elements are preserved, removed, or reported according to explicit policy
matched object elements use the same object merge conflict rules as object members
merged arrays have deterministic element ordering
JSONC comments attached to array elements have deterministic preservation or movement rules
merge reports include matched, inserted, skipped, and destination-owned element decisions
